The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500's Midgrade Trim Level Gets Split Into LT for 2WD and Z71 for 4WD
39 photos
Photo: Chevrolet
Half-ton pickup trim ladders used to be honest math a long time ago. Paying more resulted in getting more, and the badge told you from its name alone where you stood. Chevrolet made that game a little harder on the 2027 model year Silverado 1500, for the midrange Silverado grade answers to two names.
One drivetrain checkbox decides between them. Ordering two-wheel drive sees the Chevrolet brand's online configurator list it as the LT. Ticking the four-wheel-drive box on the same grade, however, turns it into the Z71. Chevrolet's built-in model comparison tool has made peace with this confusing arrangement already, labeling the trim Silverado (LT/Z71) at the moment of reporting.
This implies the Z71 package comes by default with four-wheel drive, and you are perfectly correct in this regard. Backing up to June 2026, when the Chevy division of General Motors unwrapped the next-gen truck, the plan looked much simpler. The media release from back then listed seven trims for the US market, including a brand-new middle grade called Silverado .
Chevrolet described it as being the previous LT in said press release, leaving many among us to read that as a death notice for the LT. After all, the RST and LTZ really did leave us. The Z71, on the other hand, is better known as an option package rather than a trim level.
Chevrolet welded the options in question to the grade for 2027, including off-road suspension, skid plates, and hill descent control for good measure. As opposed to the 2026 and earlier LT, the 2027 model does not offer a four-wheel-drive specification.
Photo: Chevrolet The most affordable Silverado 1500 presently configurable is the WT regular cab with the standard bed at $41,395. Stepping up to the LT means double cab and the standard bed at the very least, pushing the advertised price to $50,695 per the configurator. The Z71 with the double cab and standard bed, meanwhile, is $54,295 from the outset.
Both are listed with the enhanced TurboMax inline-four as the base engine, albeit with late availability, whereas the 5.7-liter small block has no such restrictions. The 2.7-liter turbo I4 develops 350 horsepower and 455 pound-feet (617 Newton-meters), and ships exclusively with a 10-speed automatic instead of the previous 8-speed transmission.
Displacing nearly 350 cubes, the 5.7 is a gen-six small block with 402 horsepower and 428 pound-feet (580 Newton-meters) at its disposal. Beyond these mills, prospective customers of the 2027 model year Silverado 1500 are further presented with the carryover 3.0-liter Duramax inline-six turbo diesel and a larger 6.6-liter small block.
Weirdly enough, the ZR2 off-road specification comes with the Duramax standard and the 6.6 if you prefer gasoline. The big eighter makes 481 horsepower and 501 pound-feet (679 Newton-meters), prompting General Motors to call it the most powerful naturally aspirated V8 in the segment.
The 5.7 and 6.6 small blocks replace the older 5.3 and 6.2 units, which rely on direct injection alone compared to dual injection for the gen-six engines. Oh, and by the way, Canada skipped the identity crisis altogether because the Silverado grade only comes with four-wheel drive there. As a result, the Z71 is the only midranger available in Canada.
